title: release-checkpoints-operator-journey-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures interactive UX notes and a lightweight wireframe writeup focused on the operator journey for gradual releases: checkpoints, automated rollback/fallback, and simple A/B experiments. Aim: produce a single-panel operator flow that is fast to understand, bounded in controls, and tightly instrumented for safe rollouts.

Audience:
- Product managers (console)
- Frontend engineers (release UI)
- Backend engineers (rollout service API)
- Solutions/SEs preparing runbooks for customers

TL;DR:
- Main idea: replace complex multi-step wizards with a single Release Checkpoint panel showing live health signals, an editable percentage timeline, and a visible fallback tree.
- Safe defaults: 5% canary, 10 minute stabilization window, auto-fallback to previous model after 3 failed checkpoints.
- Must show measurable signals (latency P99, error-rate, quality regression score) and the source links for examples used in rollback decisions.

High-level flow (screens / frames):
1) Release Checkpoint Overview (initial state)
   - Title: "Release: v2025.03.01 - staged rollout"
   - Key line items: target population, start time, current active percentage, next checkpoint ETA.
   - Compact sparkline row: latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate %, quality delta (compared to baseline). Each metric has a small tooltip with "why this matters" and a link to the eval prompt set.
   - Action buttons: "Pause rollout", "Advance now", "Edit checkpoints", "Abort & fallback".
   - Primary microcopy: "Use Advance to move to the next checkpoint when signals look healthy. Auto-fallback will trigger if thresholds are breached."

2) Edit Checkpoint Timeline (modal/panel)
   - UI: horizontal percent slider with discrete stops (0,1,5,10,25,50,100) and inline time buckets (e.g., 10m, 30m, 1h).
   - Each checkpoint row shows expected throughput impact and cost delta (estimated) so operator can reason about economics.
   - Inline validation: warns if gaps are greater than configured SLA window.
   - Support quick-presets: "Conservative", "Balanced", "Aggressive".

3) A/B Matrix Composer (lightweight)
   - Minimal table: variant name, model id, traffic %, measurement targets (primary metric dropdown), guardrail metrics.
   - Ability to pin baseline and two test variants. For complex experiments, link to Experiment Editor but keep rollout panel focused on operational choices.

4) Fallback Policy Editor (DSL-lite)
   - Expose commonly-used rules as toggles with human-readable preview. Example: "If error-rate increases > 2% absolute OR latency P99 increases > 200ms for two consecutive checkpoints => fallback to last-stable variant."
   - Allow schedule for progressive fallback: partial rollback to 50% before full rollback.
   - Microcopy: show example timeline of what fallback would have done historically for recent rollouts.

5) Incident & Trace Row (bottom strip persistent)
   - Shows last 6 traces sampled against the rollout, flagged SLO breaches, and the trace id quick copy button.
   - Link to observability dashboards (Grafana) and a small inline snapshot of the most representative failing request.

Interaction details and small decisions:
- Advance Now vs Auto-Advance: Provide a smart "Advance Probability" indicator (low/medium/high) based on model of signals; never auto-advance without explicit auto-advance enabled. Default onboarding sets auto-advance off.
- Pause: Immediate stop of new traffic; existing in-flight KV cache kept. Button should require single confirm.
- Abort & Fallback: Two-step modal with required reason; optional auto-open to Slack/PagerDuty template.
- Undo: Allow a 2-minute window to reverse a manual advance (soft undo). Show a countdown badge.

Accessibility and keyboard flow:
- Slider is keyboard-navigable with left/right arrows moving to next discrete stop.
- All modals focus-trap, and escape closes non-destructive modals.
- Color use: do not rely on color alone for health state — add icons and text: ✓ Healthy, ⚠️ Guardrail, ✖️ Failed.

Observability & Signals:
- Default signal set: latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate (4xx/5xx split), quality delta (eval metric), token cost per request.
- Show both absolute and delta vs baseline. Provide a small explainer line e.g., "quality delta calculated over customer prompt sample set (link)."
- Signal sources must be auditable: each metric value should have a "source" hover showing aggregation window and sampling rate.

Microcopy and confirmation language (examples):
- Primary CTA: "Advance to 10%" (if next step is 10%)
- Pause confirmation: "Pause rollout to prevent further traffic to this variant. Existing requests will continue. Continue?"
- Abort & Fallback confirmation: "Fallback will route 100% of traffic to variant 'baseline-2025-02'. This action cannot be auto-reversed. Provide reason (required)."

Wireframe component mapping (design system):
- Percentage slider -> DS RangeStepper component (discrete stops)
- Metrics sparkline row -> DS MetricsStrip with mini tooltips
- Fallback policy -> DS ToggleGroup + DS CodePreview (humaned)
- Incident row -> DS TraceSnippet with copy/links
- Toasts: short ephemeral toasts for Advance/Pause actions with undo link.

Front-end -> API mapping (examples):
- GET /rollouts/{id} -> returns rollout state, checkpoints[], metricsSummary (source url)
- PATCH /rollouts/{id}/checkpoints -> body: { "checkpoints": [{"percent":5, "duration":"10m","guardrails":[{"metric":"error_rate","threshold":0.02,"comparison":"absolute"}]}] }
- POST /rollouts/{id}/actions -> body: { "action":"advance" | "pause" | "abort", "reason": "string (required for abort)" }
- Note: keep API idempotent for advance/pause by returning canonical state and lastActionId.

Backlog grooming (near-term):
- ROLL-4510: Implement RangeStepper (UI) + keyboard support (3)
- ROLL-4511: Integrate metrics strip with metrics service + source hover (5)
- ROLL-4512: Fallback policy editor – simple toggle UI + preview (3)
- ROLL-4513: Add auto-advance boolean + onboarding defaults (2)
- ROLL-4514: Incident trace sampler & copy-to-clipboard UX (2)
- ROLL-4520: A/B matrix quick composer (5)
- ROLL-4530: Accessibility audit and keyboard e2e tests (3)
(Points in parentheses are rough story points).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How conservative should default guardrail thresholds be across customer tiers? (Enterprise may want stricter defaults.)
- Do we enable auto-advance by default for small internal rollouts? Suggest: off by default, opt-in per team.
- How to present noisy signals: smoothing vs raw? Proposal: show raw by default with a small smoothed overlay and let operators toggle smoothing.
- Audit logging: require explicit reason only for aborts, but optionally collect reasons for advances for auditability.

Runbook snippet (for SEs):
- If checkpoint fails (guardrail breach): 1) Click "Pause", 2) Inspect trace row and metric source, 3) If rollback required, choose "Abort & fallback" and select immediate fallback or staged fallback to 50% then 0%.

Mock copy for onboarding tooltip:
- "Release checkpoints guide you through a safe rollout: configure discrete stops, watch signals, and use fallback policies to automatically protect users. Try the 'Conservative' preset for most production models."

Appendix: quick visual sketches (text descriptors)
- Panel header with name + health pill (green/yellow/red).
- Main body split 60/40: left shows percent timeline and controls, right shows live metrics and A/B table.
- Bottom persistent incident row with 3-column compact trace cards.

Notes to designers/PMs:
- Keep panel discoverable under model-version detail page as "Open rollout console" rather than a separate product area.
- Prioritize first-time UX: show recommended presets and highlight the "why" for each metric.
- Aim for <3 clicks to pause or abort a rollout.

History and context:
- This is a synthesis of earlier rollout design explorations and recent customer feedback indicating confusion around when fallback triggers occur and inability to preview historical fallback impact.
- Related tickets and prototypes linked above.

Next steps:
- Review with frontend + metrics backend to validate API fields by 2025-03-09.
- Produce low-fidelity clickable prototype for internal testing by 2025-03-17.
- Schedule customer-runbook review with two pilot accounts in April.

Unresolved: attach sample baseline prompt set and short evaluation harness link in next revision.
